subject.title: [Feature]: Self-evolving SOUL.md via opt-in reflection sub-turn + soul_update tool

question: Should OpenClaw accept core, default-off SOUL.md auto-evolution, or should durable preference capture stay in memory/plugin surfaces instead?
rationale: The requested feature is missing and well-scoped, but it adds model-mediated writes to a prompt-loaded instruction file plus new config and CLI surfaces, which repository policy treats as a product and security-boundary decision.

options.title: Accept guarded core contract
options.body: Keep this issue canonical and review the linked PR only after it privately gates `soul_update`, obeys send policy, provides visible notice/undo/provenance, and covers hostile input.

options.title: Move to memory or plugin seam
options.body: Reject direct SOUL.md mutation in core and ask for durable preference capture through memory plugins or a new plugin/API extension.

options.title: Decline automatic mutation
options.body: Close this and the older overlapping issue if maintainers do not want model-mediated instruction-file writes at all.

recommendation.title: Accept guarded core contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue canonical and review the linked PR only after it privately gates `soul_update`, obeys send policy, provides visible notice/undo/provenance, and covers hostile input.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans SOUL docs, prompt assembly, plugin boundaries, and security posture, all areas where this handle appears in feature-history and architecture commits.
